- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a recent spike in price, model often overshoots and fails to capture subsequent mean reversion; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model underestimates continuation; add 2–3% to forecast for next 3–5 days to capture momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early part of 30-day horizon (days 1–7), especially when sentiment is neutral or slightly negative — increase forecast by 1–2% for first 3 days.
- When sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model lags in recognizing the shift — delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and increase slope gently.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, model tends to underestimate true price — add 3–5% to forecast for next 7–10 days to account for suppressed demand or policy effects.
